summary: Admit approval-bound Russian Post batch formation through the tenant-scoped API and durable idempotency receipt boundary.

impacts.evidence: The API resolves the connector account by the authenticated organization/workspace scope and the receipt primary key includes both tenant identifiers.
Only the normalized batch projection is stored; order references, credentials and raw provider responses remain outside the durable receipt.
OpenAPI adds POST /logistics/batches with required Idempotency-Key and Approval-Request-ID headers and a bounded request schema.
The operation returns a normalized response and does not introduce a new event or alter the event catalog.
The provider-neutral LogisticsBatchCreateRequest and LogisticsBatchCreator ports add one capability without exposing Russian Post transport types.
The existing operation_receipts schema already supports pending/completed tenant-scoped idempotency results; no migration is required.
The write-sensitive operation is default-deny, requires an enabled account capability and validates numeric remote references only at the Russian Post boundary.
The route requires an approved fulfillment.batch.create request with a request-digest-bound logistics_batch resource and write-sensitive risk.
The approval and idempotency identifiers are bound to the request digest and tenant-scoped receipt, providing a durable mutation lineage without raw provider payload.
A fresh operation receipt owns the one remote call; completed replays return the normalized result and pending receipts block automatic duplicate calls.
The connector egress call is fixed to the official HTTPS Otpravka batch endpoint; postal handoff remains outside the admitted surface.
The API distinguishes accepted pending outcomes from completed results and maps remote failures without exposing provider response bodies.
Disabling the capability or removing runtime support prevents new calls; existing pending/completed receipts remain available for reconciliation and audit.
SDK, candidate adapter, host transport, API approval/idempotency, runtime admission, OpenAPI parity and generated artifact checks cover the new operation.
